title: Edge cert rollout — evacuation & routing playbook
content:
Summary:

This note documents a safety-first evacuation + routing playbook for certificate rollouts that have the potential to cause asymmetric routing/connection failures in a regional edge deployment. It is informed by the Feb 2025 partial regional impact where a staged cert rotation combined with accelerated CDN cache expiry produced request-level TLS handshaking failures and inconsistent KV-cache lookups. Purpose is to give on-call SREs a compact checklist and decision tree to evacuate traffic safely to an alternate region or warm-standby pool while preserving client session stability and minimizing token-cost waste.

High-level objectives:
- Restore successful end-to-end requests for affected customers within SLO window (target: 3–15m depending on scope).
- Avoid heavy cold-start load on model serving (use warmed pools and KV-cache preseed where possible).
- Keep rollouts paused and provide deterministic rollback path for cert/state changes.
- Capture evidence and quick postmortem artifacts in the incident ticket.

When to use this playbook (trigger examples):
- Multiple TLS handshakes failing at edge across >3 PoPs concurrently and tracing to cert/thumbprint mismatch.
- Large rate of 4xx/5xx spikes coincident with edge config/cert deployment and DNS changes.
- Observed asymmetric behavior where some CDNs accept connections but backend rejects due to ALPN mismatch or SNI rewriting.

Quick detection checklist (first 5 minutes):
1) Confirm symptoms: aggregate metrics (edge TLS failures, LB reset, client TLS alerts).
2) Correlate with deploy window: quick check of CI/CD cert rollout job and deployment timestamps (use deploy-tracker).
3) Check BGP/route changes: verify no unexpected AS prepends or route flaps in the same timeframe.
4) Validate DNS TTLs: were TTLs lowered as part of the rollout? Are cached records expiring earlier than intended?
5) Signal for escalation: if >15% of requests in region failing or >3 customer incidents, page on-call SRE Lead.

Evacuation decision tree (short):
- If failure appears isolated to edge cert handshake errors and backend is healthy => prefer regional traffic diversion to a nearby healthy region with compatible certs.
- If large portion of regional egress is impacted or downstream model pools are degraded => escalate to cross-region evacuate and enable fallback model variants.
- If DAL (data access layer) auth tokens are failing due to cert mismatch => pause rollout, revoke problematic cert version if possible, and open emergency rollback.

Step-by-step evacuation playbook:
1) Lower DNS TTL (if we control authoritative DNS) to 30s for affected records. Command: run-admin dns-update --zone edge.redwood.ai --record *.edge --ttl 30 --reason "evacuation". Note: only do this if previous TTL was >60s and propagation is acceptable.
2) Pause cert rollout: cancel in the CD pipeline, mark the rollout job as "halted" and attach incident ticket.
3) Weighted routing shift to warm region (soft shift): adjust global routing weights to move 20% -> 50% of traffic in 1 minute increments. Use routing control API: routing-update --route edge-global --target region-us-west-2 --weight 40 --step 1m.
4) Preseed KV cache and model pool in target region: run kv-preseed --prefix /sessions/active --region us-west-2 --lookback 15m and trigger model-warmup job for top-10 models in the last hour.
5) Monitor latency and error rates for 5 minutes after each weight step. If 5xx decreases and TLS handshakes succeed, continue to next step. If not, revert last weight change and pause.
6) If weighted shift succeeds, continue progressive diversion to full evacuation to warm pool. During full evacuation, set circuit-breaker thresholds higher for cold-start retries to reduce thrash.
7) If routing change is blocked due to CDN or upstream constraints, use per-edge origin override to serve from warm region and update headers for SNI when possible.
8) After evacuation, keep cert rollout paused until root-cause debug completed and validated in staging canary environment.

Mitigation scripts & useful commands (for common setups):
- Check cert thumbprint on edge nodes: ssh edge-ops@<node> "openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -in /etc/edge/certs/current.pem"
- List active cert versions in CD: ci list-artifacts --name edge-cert --env prod
- Force pause rollout: ci cancel-pipeline --id <pipeline-id> --reason "incident SRE-7214"
- Routing rollback: routing-update --route edge-global --reset-to baseline --reason "evac rollback"

Telemetry to watch during an evacuation:
- Edge TLS handshake failures (per-PoP), client TLS alerts, and ALPN mismatches.
- 4xx/5xx rate with breakdown by CDN and PO P.
- Upstream model pool cold-start errors and qps/latency.
- KV cache hit ratio for preseeded keys in target region.
- DNS resolver error rates for customer ISPs if TTL was changed.

Post-incident follow-ups and runbook changes to add:
1) Mandatory staging canary for cert rotations across 2 control PoPs with live traffic replay before global rollout.
2) Add a preflight step to the cert rollout pipeline that verifies SNI/ALPN matrix against active CDNs and edge proxies.
3) Automated kv-preseed job that runs as part of regional failover plan; add into disaster-recovery automation repo.
4) Create a route simulation harness that models multi-CDN propagation with current TTLs and AS path variance.
5) Add a monitoring alert: "Edge: cert-thumbprint-drift" (severity P2) and a runbook link.

Incident notes (raw):
- 2025-02-18 02:12 UTC: Certificate A->B rollout started via ci/certs pipeline.
- 2025-02-18 02:16 UTC: Alert: edge-po p us-east-1 TLS handshake failures spike (sustained 4.8% of requests).
- 2025-02-18 02:20 UTC: Several customers report intermittent 521/522-like errors; initial triage saw ALPN mismatch in edge logs.
- 2025-02-18 02:23 UTC: Attempted per-node restart of edge proxy; handshake failures persisted.
- 2025-02-18 02:30 UTC: Lowered TTL to 60s for affected records to accelerate routing shift.
- 2025-02-18 02:34 UTC: Began weighted diversion to us-west-2, started KV preseed.
- 2025-02-18 02:55 UTC: Diversion completed; global errors returned to baseline by 03:05 UTC.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
- Cert rollout job propagated new certs to edge proxies, but CDN layer cache invalidation for the edge SNI metadata did not fully expire in some POPs. Combined with a fast TTL change that had already been applied by some resolvers, a subset of client connections were routed to proxies serving the new cert but where the CDN cached older origin metadata, causing TLS validation failures and backend rejects. Secondary contributing factor was that warm standby pools were not sufficiently preseeded with KV entries for active sessions, causing elevated cold-starts during the diversion.

Action items (owners):
- eng-serving-runtime: add SNI/ALPN preflight check to cert pipeline (owner: Ravi Kapoor) — due 2025-03-14.
- eng-sre: add scripted kv-preseed job and integrate it into routing-control automation (owner: Marta López) — due 2025-03-07.
- infra: add cert-thumbprint monitoring and integrate into ops-alerting (owner: Omar Haddad) — due 2025-03-10.
- product: schedule rolling deployment blackout windows to reduce risk for large customer-facing changes (owner: Priya Anand) — due 2025-03-21.

Notes to on-call: keep this doc open during any edge certificate churn. If you deviate from the playbook, capture steps in the incident timeline and link to ticket SRE-7214. When in doubt, prefer slower, weighted shifts over immediate 100% evacuation.

Appendix: quick decision grid (one-liner cheat-sheet):
- TLS-only handshake errors + healthy backends = weighted region diversion + KV preseed.
- Backend auth/token failures = pause rollout + emergency rollback.
- CDN cache inconsistent with origin = force cache purge + pause, or route around affected PoPs.

End of document.
